detail.tagline: A few minutes a day, scheduled so words stick.
overview: An offline-capable progressive web app that turns 425 words collected since 2020 into a daily habit. Each day it builds a short session of words that are due plus a handful of new ones, and schedules every word's next appearance from how well you knew it.

A home dashboard shows today's progress ring, the session size and time, a weekly streak and a word of the day; the whole app is still regenerated from a single JSON file by a Python build step, with progress kept on the device.
highlights: Daily sessions: due words plus a few new ones, about three minutes
SM-2-style scheduling — three grades, intervals that stretch as words stick
Home dashboard with a progress ring, weekly streak and word of the day
425 words spanning 2020–2026, with the newest meanings corrected
Add a word from the phone and it's in the catalogue immediately
Generated from one JSON file — the repo is the database

items.benefit: Turns maths drills into something kids ask to play — with daily missions, streaks and collectable pets that bring them back each day.

detail.tagline: Blocky monsters, real maths — a quiz game kids want to play.
overview: Block Math (ブロックさんすう) started life as a wave-survival shooter and was rebuilt as a maths game for kids: each mob carries a question pitched at a school grade, and answering it correctly on the on-screen number pad is what defeats it.

A layer of light progression keeps it going between sessions — combos, a permanent level, daily missions, a play streak, achievements and collectable pets that walk beside the player — while the arena changes biome as the grade rises. It is still a single HTML file with no build step.

items.name: Wellbeing Navi
items.description: A private, on-device robo-advisor in the WealthNavi style — risk profiling, portfolio construction, Monte-Carlo projections and rebalancing suggestions for the family.
items.benefit: Brings robo-advisor intelligence to the family's investing while keeping every byte of financial data encrypted on your own devices.

detail.tagline: A WealthNavi-style robo-advisor that never leaves your device.
overview: Wellbeing Navi replicates the intelligence of a robo-advisor — risk profiling, mean-variance portfolio construction, Monte-Carlo projections, market-aware recommendations and rebalancing suggestions — as a private tool for the family.

It deliberately stays a decision-support tool (you place every trade yourself at your own broker), and all data lives in an AES-256-GCM encrypted vault on your own devices: a desktop app on the Mac, and phones over home Wi-Fi.

A tax module now estimates cross-border returns with a CSV worksheet for an accountant, and a security pass raised the vault's key derivation to 600,000 iterations and added guards against doctored or AI-generated statements: any imported balance that moves a figure by more than a quarter has to be confirmed twice.
highlights: Risk profiling and mean-variance portfolio construction
Monte-Carlo projections and recurring-investment planning
Rebalancing suggestions that track the market
Everything encrypted on-device — no server, no account
Desktop app plus phone access over home Wi-Fi

Guards against doctored or AI-generated statements: large changes need a second confirmation

items.description: A Brookhaven-style scavenger-hunt game set in a full Three.js city — dozens of missions tracking down the hidden "67", with shops, vehicles, outfits and crime events.
items.benefit: Gives the kids a Roblox-style world of their own — playable together on Mac, iPad or iPhone, straight from the browser.

detail.tagline: Find the 67 — a scavenger hunt across a whole city.
overview: A mysterious "67" hides somewhere in a full Brookhaven-style metropolis — downtown, mall, stadium, farm, marina, funfair, two climbable mountains and an island offshore. Read the clues, track it down, and strike the legendary 67 pose.

Forty missions (and counting) mix classic hunts with citizen interviews and random crime events; coins earned catching thieves buy bikes, boats, jetpacks and outfits, each unlocking bonus events. Friends join the same city through multiplayer rooms, and progress auto-saves in the browser. Built as a Three.js prototype to port to Roblox Studio.

Since then the world has grown south to Lake Suwa — a mountain lake with a torii in the water, a tiled-roof Japanese house to explore and dragonflies to sneak up on — and a sports corner now hosts TABLE TENNIS 67, a first-person match with six strokes and a real arc over the net. A home-building loop grades your plot, and a What's New panel tracks every update.
highlights: A ~1200×1200-stud living city with townsfolk, traffic and wildlife
40 missions: hunts, citizen interviews, and thief chases
67 Shop: bicycle, motorboat, jetpack and outfits with bonus events

40 のミッションは、王道の宝さがしから住民への聞き込み、突発的な犯人追跡まで。泥棒を捕まえて得たコインで自転車・ボート・ジェットパック・衣装を買うと、それぞれ専用のイベントが開きます。友だちとは合言葉で同じ街に集合でき、進み具合はブラウザに自動保存。Roblox Studio への移植を見据えた Three.js 版です。
その後、世界は南の諏訪湖まで広がりました。湖の中に鳥居が立つ山の湖、探検できる瓦屋根の日本家屋、そっと近づいて捕まえるトンボ。スポーツコーナーには、6 種類の打ち方と本物の放物線でネットを越える一人称の TABLE TENNIS 67 も加わりました。家づくりは区画を採点してくれるようになり、「What's New」でアップデートの履歴も見られます。

items.description: A nightly automation that aggregates for-sale listings from Tokyo, Saitama, Tsukuba and Karuizawa property portals into one dashboard, tracking new listings, price drops and flood risk.
items.benefit: Surfaces new listings and price drops across several portals and cities each morning — with flood-risk and green-space filtering, and delisted listings verified before they're removed — instead of checking sites by hand.

detail.tagline: A nightly watch over Tokyo & Karuizawa property listings.
overview: 物件ウォッチ collects for-sale listings from Japanese property portals — SUUMO, LIFULL HOME'S, 三井のリハウス, cowcamo — into one self-contained HTML dashboard, checking nightly for anything new.

Every listing is normalised onto one schema, diffed against a local store so a listing is "new" exactly once, and price changes are kept as history rather than overwritten. The search has grown since launch: more cities (including Saitama and Tsukuba), a green-space proximity score, flood-risk filtering, and stricter verification before a listing is ever marked delisted.
highlights: Nightly incremental run at 02:00, plus a deeper weekly full sweep

Green-space proximity score and flood-risk filtering added to the search
Normalises Japanese price, area and walk-time formats onto one schema
Price drops tracked as history, not overwritten — with a dedicated badge and tab
Every delisted listing is re-verified before removal, not just assumed sold

items.name: YouTube Summarizer
items.description: A phone-to-Mac relay that turns YouTube videos into searchable notes: share a video from the phone, and a Mac at home transcribes and summarises it into a personal library.
items.benefit: Captures a video in one tap from the phone's Share sheet and turns it into notes you can search and ask follow-up questions about later — without the video being downloaded.

detail.tagline: Share a video from the phone; read the notes later.
overview: What began as a command-line summariser is now a small system: an iOS Share-sheet shortcut sends a video link to a job queue in the cloud, and an agent on a Mac at home picks it up, has it transcribed in a Gemini Notebook, and writes back a transcript plus simple and detailed summaries.

A key-gated phone portal lists the whole library with search, shows job progress, and lets you ask follow-up questions about any one video — each answered from that video alone. The original command-line tool and Claude Code skill still work alongside it.
highlights: One tap from the iOS Share sheet, via a signed shortcut
A cloud job queue with stages, retries and an agent-online indicator
The Mac only makes outbound requests — its sign-in never leaves the machine
Searchable library plus per-video follow-up questions
Jobs submitted while the Mac sleeps simply wait in the queue
Key-gated portal: anyone without the key gets a plain 404

architecture.summary: The work happens on a Mac at home, but the Mac is never exposed: a small Cloudflare Worker holds a job queue and the library, the phone talks only to the Worker, and the Mac polls the Worker outbound for work. The Worker never talks to Google.

items.name: MyPoi
items.description: A dashboard that gathers a dozen loyalty-point and mile accounts into one comic-panel view — balances collected automatically, with expiry countdowns and earn/spend history.
items.benefit: Turns scattered point balances into one glance, collected on a schedule, with an expiry countdown so points don't quietly lapse unused.

detail.tagline: One dashboard for every loyalty point balance.
overview: A personal dashboard that combines a dozen point and mile accounts into one running total, now redrawn as manga panels — bold outlines, a speech-bubble total and a pace badge that compares this month with the last.

A collector now visits each site on its own, reusing a browser profile the owner signed into once by hand, and reads balances, expiring points and history without ever handling a password. Sites whose terms forbid automation stay manual-entry, and the portal stays key-gated: without the key, every request gets a plain 404.
highlights: Balances collected automatically from a once-signed-in browser profile — no passwords stored
Reads by text label rather than page layout, and refuses to record low-confidence numbers
Sites whose terms forbid automation are kept manual, by design
Earn and spend history, de-duplicated, alongside the monthly net change
Manga-panel interface with inline-SVG charts and no external libraries
Key-gated, with a hash-pinned CSP — without the key, a plain 404

images.caption: The manga-panel redesign, shown with the app's built-in demo data

architecture.summary: The owner signs into each site once in a visible browser; from then on a Playwright collector reuses that profile headlessly, reads the numbers, and sends them to a small Worker in one authenticated write. The phone portal reads from the Worker. Manual entry still works alongside the collector.

items.name: 67 Password
items.description: An offline, single-user password manager for iPhone built on a two-secret key-derivation design — parked after its encrypted core and iOS interface were complete.
items.benefit: Shows what a zero-knowledge vault takes to build properly: every field encrypted, keys that never leave the device, and 156 tests against published cryptographic test vectors.

detail.tagline: A zero-knowledge password vault for iPhone — parked, not abandoned.
overview: 67 Password is an offline password manager for iPhone, written in Swift 6 and SwiftUI with no third-party dependencies. The vault key is derived from two secrets — a master password and a device-held Secret Key — and every item, including its title and username, is stored encrypted in a local SQLite database.

The encrypted core, a test suite of 156 checks and the main iOS screens (onboarding, Face ID unlock, items, search, generator, settings) were finished before the project was parked: system-wide AutoFill needs a paid developer membership, which outweighed the benefit for a single user.
highlights: Two-secret key derivation: master password plus a device-held Secret Key
AES-256-GCM for every item, bound to its slot so ciphertexts can't be swapped
156 unit tests against published RFC vectors, plus a full UI acceptance run
Password generator (random, memorable, PIN), strength meter and built-in one-time codes
Face ID unlock, auto-lock and a clipboard that expires
Status: parked after phase 2 of 9 — no network code at all

images.caption: First launch — encrypted on the device, no servers, no subscriptions

architecture.summary: Everything runs on the device. Two secrets are stretched and combined into an account key, which unlocks a random vault key, which in turn decrypts each item on demand. Nothing is stored in the clear — not even item titles — and there is no network code.

flow.note: The Secret Key never leaves the device's Keychain

flow.note: A random 256-bit key, itself stored encrypted

flow.note: AES-256-GCM with each ciphertext bound to its own slot

ja.description: 2 つの秘密情報による鍵導出で作った、オフライン・個人用の iPhone 向けパスワードマネージャー。暗号化の中核と iOS 画面が完成した段階で一時停止。
ja.benefit: ゼロ知識の保管庫をきちんと作るとどうなるかを示します。すべての項目を暗号化し、鍵は端末から出さず、公開された暗号テストベクタに対して 156 のテストで検証しています。

detail.tagline: iPhone のためのゼロ知識パスワード保管庫 — 中断中、放棄ではなく。
overview: 67 Password は、Swift 6 と SwiftUI で書いた iPhone 向けのオフライン・パスワードマネージャーです。外部ライブラリは使っていません。保管庫の鍵はマスターパスワードと端末に保存された Secret Key の 2 つから導き、タイトルやユーザー名を含むすべての項目を暗号化してローカルの SQLite に保存します。
暗号化の中核、156 のテスト、主要な iOS 画面（初回設定、Face ID ロック解除、項目、検索、パスワード生成、設定）まで完成したところで一時停止しました。システム全体の自動入力には有料の開発者メンバーシップが必要で、1 人で使うには割に合わなかったためです。
highlights: 2 つの秘密による鍵導出：マスターパスワード＋端末の Secret Key
すべての項目を AES-256-GCM で暗号化。保存先に紐付け、暗号文の入れ替えを防止
公開 RFC のテストベクタに対する 156 の単体テストと、UI 全体の受け入れテスト
パスワード生成（ランダム・覚えやすい・PIN）、強度メーター、ワンタイムコード内蔵
Face ID でのロック解除、自動ロック、時間で消えるクリップボード
現状：全 9 段階のうち 2 段階目で一時停止。通信コードは一切なし

architecture.summary: すべてが端末上で完結します。2 つの秘密を引き伸ばして組み合わせたアカウント鍵が、ランダムな保管庫の鍵を開き、その鍵で各項目を必要なときだけ復号します。項目のタイトルさえ平文では保存せず、通信のコードもありません。
